chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Zayyat from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) gave a ruling regarding the hermaphrodite (khuntha): he has the share of men and he has the share of women. He said: He is inherited from where he urinates. If both come out together, then from where came out first. If they came out equally, then from where the stream originates. If they are equal, he inherits the inheritance of both men and women.
ai.seo_question: How is the inheritance share of a hermaphrodite determined in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes a physiological criterion for determining the inheritance share of a hermaphrodite (khuntha), prioritizing the organ that excretes urine first to resolve ambiguity. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of relying on observable physical signs to assign gender-specific rights when biological sex is indeterminate. The detailed hierarchy of urination streams ensures precise allocation of inheritance, balancing both male and female shares in cases of equal output.
